{"findings":[{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N4","page":1,"quote":"4) $FLASH HARD CHROME PLATING 15 TO 20 MICRONS,HARDNESS 850."},{"kind":"note","ref":"N1","page":1,"quote":"1)#USE STD. DIA.35g6 En-8(D) BRIGHT BAR."}],"comment":"Note N4 specifies flash hard chrome plating of 15–20 microns, but note N1 calls out a 35g6 shaft diameter whose tolerance band (0.025 mm) is tighter than the plating thickness; without allowance for the coating the finished shaft will be oversize and the g6 fit will not function. The designer must either reduce the pre-plate machining size by the plating thickness or add a note stating the g6 applies after plating."

,
"recommended_correction":"Reduce the nominal machined diameter by the plating thickness so that the final plated size meets 35g6, or explicitly state that the g6 tolerance applies after plating."},{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N4","page":1,"quote":"4) $FLASH HARD CHROME PLATING 15 TO 20 MICRONS,HARDNESS 850."},{"kind":"note","ref":"N7","page":1,"quote":"KEY WAY DIMENSION ADDED & HEAT TREATMENT NOTE REMOVED"}],"comment":"Note N4 requires hardness 850 (presumably HV) for the chrome plate, yet no heat treatment or hardness is specified for the En-8(D) substrate, and note N7 confirms the heat-treatment note was deliberately removed; a hard chrome layer on an untreated medium-carbon steel shaft risks spalling under load because the base material lacks adequate core strength. The designer must specify the required heat treatment and hardness for the shaft body and state at which manufacturing stage it applies."

,
"recommended_correction":"Add a heat-treatment note specifying the process, target hardness, and the stage in the manufacturing sequence at which it is to be performed."}]}
